title: Best Golf Gloves UK
short: Nine tested golf gloves compared on grip, feel, wet-weather performance and durability, from the tour-standard FootJoy StaSof to a synthetic glove that encourages a lighter grip.
intro: A golf glove is the only part of your body in constant contact with the club, so grip, feel and durability matter more than they look on a shelf. This guide compares gloves tested by Golf Monthly's team, who used each over a number of rounds and in different conditions, judging grip over time, wet and dry performance, fit and how well the glove wears. Testing is spread across golfers of different abilities so fit and feel are covered fairly.

products.name: StaSof Glove
products.best_for: Golfers who want a proven all-weather glove
products.key_spec: Premium Cabretta leather, Powernet mesh back, All-climate grip with APL palm leather, sizes S-3XL
products.summary: A staple of the professional tours for decades, and Golf Monthly's top pick for its super-soft leather and mesh section that keeps the hand cool. Moisture management was excellent on warm days and the All-climate grip and APL leather palm cope with light rain, while it snugly and comfortably fits a range of hands. The only downside noted is that it comes in one colour.

specs.Key tech: Powernet mesh back, All-climate grip, APL palm leather

pros: Excellent moisture management, copes with light rain

products.name: Tour Preferred Glove
products.best_for: Golfers who want a thin, tacky, pro-endorsed leather glove
products.key_spec: AAA Cabretta Soft Tech leather, moisture-wicking wristband, snug closure, sizes S-XL
products.summary: Worn on tour by players such as Collin Morikawa and Charley Hull, this uses a super-thin AAA Cabretta leather with a noticeable tackiness that helps grip. Golf Monthly found the wristband wicks moisture away well and the closure gives a truly snug fit, in a simple, elegant design, though there are limited breathing holes.
pros: High quality leather with a tacky feel

products.name: Golf Glove
products.best_for: Golfers who want fit and feel plus colours beyond traditional white
products.key_spec: AA Cabretta leather, seam and perforation placement for fit, sizes S-2XL
products.summary: A newcomer to gloves compared with FootJoy, but Golf Monthly found fit and feel are on point, with exceptionally soft AA Cabretta leather giving great feel and comfort, and clever seam and perforation placement aiding the fit. There are plenty of brighter colours, including camo, but it isn't good in wet weather.

products.name: Original Series Golf Glove
products.best_for: Golfers who prize quality stitching and feel, including juniors and women's fits
products.key_spec: Premium soft leather, youth, cadet, standard and women's sizes, sold as a two-pack
products.summary: Golf Monthly found this superbly made, with incredibly soft, supple leather that feels luxurious and quality stitching throughout. It comes in some brighter colours such as mint and pink, and youth, cadet, standard and women's sizes, but it's only sold as a two-pack, so it makes sense to be sure of the fit before buying.

specs.Sizes: Youth XXS-XL, Cadet S-XXL, Standard S-XXL, Women's S-L

pros: Wide size range including youth and women's
cons: Has to be bought as a two-pack

products.name: Tour Authentic Glove
products.best_for: Golfers who want a tacky, tour-developed glove for dry conditions
products.key_spec: Soft leather with Griptac technology, moisture-wicking cuff, sizes S-XL
products.summary: Developed with feedback from many Callaway staff players, this soft leather glove uses Griptac tech that Golf Monthly found does its job well, with excellent feel and control. Comfort is high thanks to the moisture-wicking cuff, snug closure and cleverly placed perforations, but it isn't great in wetter weather.
pros: Excellent feel and control, comfortable cuff

products.name: Tour Edition Glove
products.best_for: Golfers who want a stylish glove that lasts
products.key_spec: Premium soft leather, many colours and styles, sizes S-XL
products.summary: Golf Monthly's tester was impressed with the durability of this leather glove, unusual among leather gloves, alongside soft, comfortable premium leather and a stylish design in many colours and styles at an attractive price. The one fault was that the thumb came up a fraction short.
cons: Thumb came up a fraction short for the testers

products.name: Ultimate Leather Glove
products.best_for: Golfers who want a soft Cabretta glove with good ventilation
products.key_spec: 100% premium Cabretta leather, perforations under the fingers, sizes S-XL
products.summary: Golf Monthly found the Cabretta leather soft with excellent grip and performance, and was particularly taken with perforations beneath the fingers, which performed superbly for breathability and aided grip. It may fit a little smaller than other top models, so check sizing, and it scuffed on the palm after a few rounds.
cons: Scuffed on the palm after a few rounds
May come up a little smaller than other top models

products.name: Players Glove
products.best_for: Golfers who want timeless looks and superb feel from thin Cabretta leather
products.key_spec: Super thin premium Cabretta leather, seams placed away from the grip, satin reinforcement at cuff and thumb, sizes S-XL
products.summary: Golf Monthly found timeless aesthetics and super thin, tried-and-tested Cabretta leather giving superb feel and plenty of comfort, with seams positioned so they don't interfere with the grip. It's durable enough thanks to satin reinforcements around the cuff and thumb, though it isn't waterproof.
pros: Seams designed not to interfere with grip

products.name: Relaxgrip 2.0 DX Glove
products.best_for: Golfers who grip the club too tightly
products.key_spec: Japanese synthetic fabric, dual expansion zone for the thumb, anatomical palm and finger pads, sizes S-3XL
products.summary: The outlier in the guide: a synthetic glove with a dual expansion zone that adjusts to any thumb length or width and anatomical pads in the palm and fingers. Golf Monthly's tester didn't need to apply as much grip pressure, which took a while to get used to but reduced tension in the hands and forearms, though the feel won't be for everyone.
cons: Feel won't be for everyone, takes time to get used to

guide.q: Which hand do I wear a golf glove on?
guide.a: A right-handed golfer with a conventional grip typically wears the glove on their left hand, because the left is the lead hand in the swing. Left-handed golfers wear it on the right hand.

Most gloves here use Cabretta leather, prized for its soft, thin feel and tackiness, though leather can scuff (as the adidas did) and some, like the G/Fore, Callaway and Titleist, aren't good in wet weather. A synthetic glove such as the Bionic Relaxgrip trades leather feel for extra features and a lighter-grip effect.

guide.q: Which glove is best in the rain?
guide.a: In Golf Monthly's main test the FootJoy StaSof coped with light showers thanks to its All-climate grip and APL palm leather, whereas the G/Fore, Callaway Tour Authentic and Titleist Players were flagged as weaker in wet weather. Golf Monthly also runs a separate guide to rain gloves.

guide.q: How should a golf glove fit?
guide.a: Snug but comfortable, without wrinkling across the palm or restricting your fingers. Sizing varies between brands: Golf Monthly found the adidas comes up a little smaller than other top models, and the Skins glove's thumb came up slightly short, so check each brand's size guide before buying.
